image.subject: A forensic archaeologist in a white field jacket kneels at the edge of a neat square trench cut into a lawn beside a timber house, a string grid over the dirt and a labelled plastic evidence bag set on a tarp beside her

storyboard.claim: Forensic dating proves one of the skeletons is only about fifty years old, so it belongs to the modern family.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An archaeologist working a grid in a yard trench beside the house, with an evidence bag labelled for lab testing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the forensic phase after the earth-doesn't-lie setup.
storyboard.addedInformation: The trench and grid show the bones were excavated methodically, not guessed at.

image.subject: Molly, a young woman in her twenties, plain build, brown hair under a cap, rough servant's dress, stands in the doorway of a dim timber kitchen with her arms at her sides and a guarded stare

storyboard.claim: Molly is the female skeleton, a servant who was murdered by Caroline three centuries ago.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Molly alone in a plain servant's dress and cap, guarded and watchful, in a timber doorway.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts a face to the female skeleton the forensics just identified.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her rough dress and cap mark her as the servant, not the mistress.

image.subject: Caroline, a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, stands at the chestnut front door of a timber house in winter, a worn travelling bundle at her feet

storyboard.claim: Caroline comes back from exile twenty-five years after Molly's death, to the house she is about to be accused from.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline at the heavy front door, a bundle at her feet, frightened eyes on the house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the second woman's return, the link that makes the female skeleton's death a murder.
storyboard.addedInformation: The travelling bundle and the closed door show she has come home to a place that is not safe.

storyboard.claim: The narrator announces that the male skeleton is the final twist, and pauses to start the reveal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain text card, no picture, marking the pause before the reveal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transition from the female skeleton into the male one.
storyboard.addedInformation: Nothing new visually; it is banter that sets up the reveal.

storyboard.claim: The viewer's assumption is that the male skeleton is Jonas Reef, the serial killer, and that he finally got justice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question card asking whether the killer finally gets justice.
storyboard.onScreenText: Did the killer finally get justice?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the assumption the next beat will overturn.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question frames the reveal as a moral one that the reader expects.

image.subject: A man in his fifties, heavy build, dark wool coat, white collar, stern face, stands alone in a backyard at dusk beside a freshly turned patch of dirt, a spade leaning against the timber wall of the house

storyboard.claim: Archie would have killed Jonas and buried him in the yard to protect the family name.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Archie in the yard at dusk beside turned earth and a spade, stern and alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the assumed story the question in the last beat described.
storyboard.addedInformation: The spade and fresh soil set up the burial the epilogue later reveals to be the wrong body.

storyboard.claim: The reader must remember the epilogue, where Jonas Reef survived.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A text card reading the epilogue line, as if a page from the book.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Overturns the assumption from the question card with the epilogue fact.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the one fact that breaks the assumed ending.

image.subject: A man in his fifties, heavy build, dark wool coat, white collar, stern face, sits alone at the head of a long candlelit dining table laid with silver, in a panelled room of the house

storyboard.claim: Jonas took Archie's identity and lived out his life in Archie's bed, clothes and house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A man wearing Archie's dark coat and white collar seated at the head of Archie's table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the survivor in the place of the victim the epilogue describes.
storyboard.addedInformation: The silver and candles show how comfortably he lived in the stolen household.

image.subject: A frost-covered backyard at first light beside a timber house, a shallow unmarked mound of cold dirt near the foot of the wall with no stone or marker

storyboard.claim: The male skeleton in the backyard is the real Archie, left in an unmarked grave for three hundred years.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A frosted yard at dawn with an unmarked grave mound by the house wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Replaces the impostor on the screen with the real body in the ground.
storyboard.addedInformation: The missing marker shows that the murdered man was never honoured.

image.subject: A young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, stands in a candlelit hallway of the house with one hand on a closed door, her face in shadow

storyboard.claim: Archie was murdered in his own home by his wife Caroline and her lover so they could take his identity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline in a dim hallway, hand on a shut door, face half in shadow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the killer in the house the grave is in.
storyboard.addedInformation: The closed door and shadow show the crime happened inside the family home.

image.subject: A young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, looks out of a low bedroom window at night, the dark grounds of the estate beyond the glass

storyboard.claim: Caroline and her lover wanted to steal Archie's identity to keep the house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline at a low bedroom window at night, watching the dark grounds.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the motive for the murder the last beat showed.
storyboard.addedInformation: The window onto the grounds is the house's boundary she wants to keep.

image.subject: A man in his fifties, heavy build, dark wool coat, white collar, stern face, stands before a half-finished timber frame house in an open field, a surveyor's rope and stakes in the grass at his feet

storyboard.claim: Archie was the wealthy merchant who built the house and founded the town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Archie beside the raw timber frame of the house, rope and stakes in the grass.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains who the murdered man was in the family's history.
storyboard.addedInformation: The surveying rope shows him as a founder who laid out the land.

image.subject: A formal oil portrait of a man in a dark wool coat and white collar hangs above a stone fireplace in a candlelit parlour, dust on its gilt frame and the room otherwise empty

storyboard.claim: The killer's portrait was painted and hung in the parlour for three centuries, while the real Archie lay in the dirt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A formal portrait of a man in Archie's coat above a parlour fireplace, dust on the frame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the impostor honoured in the house while the real man is in the yard.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dust on the frame shows how long the portrait has hung untouched.

image.subject: A seventeenth-century timber house at night in fog, its windows dark except for one candle, the iron-fronted street side of the house lit faintly from within

storyboard.claim: The house consumed its own creator, and it always keeps the records of what happened on its land.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The timber house at night in fog, one candle in a window, its iron-fronted side lit faintly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the individual crimes to the house as the thing holding them.
storyboard.addedInformation: The single candle shows the house keeping its own secret in the dark.

image.subject: The heavy chestnut front door of a timber house, closed, with an iron bear knocker at its centre, in flat afternoon light

storyboard.claim: The location of Peton protected the killers and hid the bodies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The shut chestnut door with the iron bear knocker, flat and closed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the house-as-keeper idea with its literal shield.
storyboard.addedInformation: The iron bear knocker is the house's shield motif in close view.

storyboard.claim: The narrator admits he loves the thematic weight of the book, and then turns to a caveat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain text card, no picture, marking the turn to critique.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ends the praise and starts the critical section.
storyboard.addedInformation: Nothing new visually; it is a verbal turn.

storyboard.claim: The narrator asks the viewer to look at the mechanics of the writing and not only the themes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question card asking whether the twist is believable.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from the praised theme to the craft question.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question tells the viewer the praise is about to be tested.

image.subject: Celia, a woman in her seventies, composed, grey-streaked hair, cardigan, cold expression, sits beside Ethel, an elderly woman in her eighties, thin, grey hair in a bun, dark cardigan, stern face, in a plain bedroom, the two of them side by side on a bed

storyboard.claim: The Celia and Ethel twist in the modern story asks for a huge suspension of disbelief.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Celia and Ethel seated together on a bed in a plain bedroom, the two women close and unreadable.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the two women of the modern twist on screen for the critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: Their closeness shows the impersonation the critique is about.

image.subject: A cracked old oak beam running across the low timber ceiling of a candlelit room, shot from below, a long split in its grain

storyboard.claim: The twist is the weakest structural beam in the book, and the book leans on the dementia trope to hold it up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cracked oak beam across a low timber ceiling, shot from below.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Uses the structure metaphor to introduce the weakness.
storyboard.addedInformation: The split in the beam is a physical picture of the failing structure.

image.subject: Ethel, an elderly woman in her eighties, thin, grey hair in a bun, dark cardigan, stern face, sits in an armchair holding knitting needles and stares blankly at nothing across the room

storyboard.claim: The book hides its clues behind the grandmother's dementia, and her confusion is the cover.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ethel in an armchair, knitting needles in hand, staring blankly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the grandmother on screen as the author's cover story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her blank stare shows the confusion the author uses as cover.

storyboard.claim: The clues the author uses to hide the twist are the confused knitting, the panic bursts and Letty calling Julia.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A text list of three clues, no picture.
storyboard.onScreenText: CONFUSED KNITTING / SUDDEN PANIC / LETTY CALLS JULIA
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists the clues the dementia cover hides behind.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the three specific clues the critique is pointing at.

image.subject: Julia, a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, stands in a dim timber hallway with her arms folded, looking past the camera at an elderly woman in a dark cardigan who has shrunk back against the wall

storyboard.claim: The grandmother's panic is a convenient way for the author to explain away large logic gaps.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia in a dim hallway, arms folded, watching an elderly woman shrink back against the wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the clues into the reader's view through Julia.
storyboard.addedInformation: Julia's tired stare shows the reader's suspicion of the excuse.

image.subject: Celia, a woman in her seventies, composed, grey-streaked hair, cardigan, cold expression, stands at a bedroom mirror pinning her grey hair into a bun, a framed photograph of an elderly woman propped on the dresser beside her

storyboard.claim: It is hard to believe Celia impersonated Ethel for over fifty years.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Celia at a mirror pinning her hair into Ethel's bun, an old photograph on the dresser.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the impersonation the question in the narration asks about.
storyboard.addedInformation: The photograph on the dresser is the model she is copying.

image.subject: A holiday dinner table set for a family in a candlelit dining room of the house, a row of chairs drawn up with one chair empty and the candles burned low

storyboard.claim: No outside family came for holidays and noticed a discrepancy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A set holiday table in the candlelit dining room, one empty chair.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the family gathering on screen that the claim says nobody saw through.
storyboard.addedInformation: The empty chair hints at people who were present but did not notice.

storyboard.claim: No doctors, dentists or bank tellers noticed that the woman was an impostor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A text list of three professions, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists who should have noticed, after the holiday visitors.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the specific professions whose records would have exposed her.

storyboard.claim: Fifty years of aging, records, x-rays, blood work and DNA would all expose the impersonation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A large number card reading fifty years, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Quantifies the time the impersonation had to survive.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fifty-year figure makes the scale of the improbability concrete.

image.subject: The iron-fronted street side of a timber house in the small town of Wood Haven, townspeople walking past on the cobbled street without looking up at the house

storyboard.claim: Nobody in the town of Wood Haven flagged the impostor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The iron-fronted house front with townspeople walking past without a glance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the family to the wider town that also failed to notice.
storyboard.addedInformation: The passers-by ignoring the house show how the town looked away.

storyboard.claim: The reader must accept two impossible things: a complicit town and flawless acting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A text checklist of two impossible items, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the two premises the critique says the reader must swallow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the logical cost of the twist as two items to accept.

storyboard.claim: The estate's isolation was so complete that Ethel never had to produce a valid ID for five decades.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A text card reading the missing identification as if from a file.
storyboard.onScreenText: No valid ID for five decades.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the one document the impersonation never had to pass.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the missing paperwork that would have exposed the fraud.

image.subject: Molly, a young woman in her twenties, plain build, brown hair under a cap, rough servant's dress, stands in a candlelit kitchen wearing a dark wool coat with a white collar that is far too large for her, her chin raised

storyboard.claim: A servant taking the life of her master parallels the 1692 story, though it fails as a realistic plot.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Molly in a dark wool coat and white collar far too large for her, chin raised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the servant in the master's clothes the thematic claim describes.
storyboard.addedInformation: The oversized coat is the visual proof of the swap the narrator is calling parallel.

image.subject: Julia, a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, sits at a bare kitchen table in a modern room under a single lamp, reading a paperback with a frown

storyboard.claim: As a grounded real-world thriller, the plot asks the reader to look the other way on modern logistics.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia at a kitchen table under a lamp, reading a paperback with a frown.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the critique into the modern present with Julia as the reader.
storyboard.addedInformation: Julia's frown shows the reader's doubt about the logistics.

image.subject: Julia, a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, turns her face away from an open book on a bedroom table with her eyes shut

storyboard.claim: The reader must deliberately look away from basic modern logistics.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia turning her face from an open book, eyes shut.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the frown from the last beat into a deliberate look away.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her shut eyes show the choice the reader has to make.

image.subject: A paperback lying open face-down on a low bedside table beside a single lit candle, a window onto the dark grounds behind it, the room late at night

storyboard.claim: The twist is thrilling at midnight, but it asks a huge favour of the reader.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An open paperback face-down beside a candle, a window onto the dark grounds.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the reader's frown to the late-night experience of reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: The candle and dark window set the midnight mood the narrator describes.

image.subject: A formal family portrait in a candlelit parlour: a man in his fifties, heavy build, dark wool coat, white collar, stern face, stands beside a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, both looking straight ahead

storyboard.claim: The book's theme of what a family will do to keep its house is strong enough that the reader forgives the flaws.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A formal portrait of Archie and Caroline in a candlelit parlour, both looking straight ahead.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the family theme that the forgiveness claim rests on.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stiff, paired portrait shows the family the book is about.

image.subject: A cold frost-covered yard beside a timber house at dawn, with three shallow dug holes in the dirt marked by wooden pegs and string between them, no bodies visible

storyboard.claim: The three buried people in the yard are the real Ethel, the real Molly and the real Archie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A frosted yard with three shallow excavated holes marked by pegs and string.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the yard with the three graves the narrator names.
storyboard.addedInformation: The pegs and string show the three graves measured and recorded.

image.subject: The front facade of a seventeenth-century timber house at night, its heavy chestnut door and iron bear knocker lit by a single lantern, with a low mound of fresh soil at the foot of its wall

storyboard.claim: They did not bury the bodies to keep the house; they buried them to become the house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The house front at night with a lantern, the door, and a mound of soil at the wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the final answer as the house itself, with the graves at its foundation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The soil against the wall shows the bodies now part of the building.

left.label: THE ELDRIDGES
left.subject: A stern man in a dark wool coat and white collar stands before a heavy chestnut door, looking out at the viewer

right.label: PETON
right.subject: A seventeenth-century timber house at dusk, its windows lit and its door shut, the walls seeming to hold its family inside

storyboard.claim: Peton does not belong to the Eldridge family; the Eldridge family belongs to Peton.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A split comparison: a stern man at the chestnut door on the left, the timber house at dusk on the right.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the chunk by reversing the ownership the whole segment has built.
storyboard.addedInformation: The side-by-side makes the reversal of ownership visible to a muted viewer.
